CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

file.content:
# Install Provenance

Released Entire CLI binaries may include installer-owned provenance at:

- `~/.config/entire/install.json`

The CLI treats this file as read-only. Installers are responsible for creating
and updating it. The CLI may fall back to legacy heuristics when the file is
missing for backwards compatibility.

## File format

Example:

```json
{
  "manager": "brew",
  "channel": "nightly",
  "package": "entire@nightly",
  "installed_at": "2026-04-11T12:00:00Z"
}
```

Fields:

- `manager`: installer identity such as `install.sh`, `brew`, or `scoop`
- `channel`: release channel such as `stable` or `nightly`
- `package`: installer-native package identifier used for update commands
- `installed_at`: RFC3339 UTC timestamp written by the installer

## Update mapping

The CLI derives update hints from provenance:

- `install.sh` + `stable` -> `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
- `brew` + `stable|nightly` -> `brew upgrade <package>`
- `scoop` + `stable|nightly` -> `scoop update <package>`

If provenance is absent, the CLI may infer a legacy update hint from the
executable path.

message.content:
I do want to add an auto update mechanisims. Something like codex has, once they detect there is a new version it prompts you something like:
New version detected. Do you want to install it? Y/N 

And it runs the command needed to update it, bash install/brew upgrade/scoop upgrade, depending of what kind of release you have, posix stable or nightly or windows.
What is the simpest way to get that done? I want to have the best UX experience.

content.text:
Simplest: keep the existing `CheckAndNotify` silent-on-error shape, but when `updateCommand()` resolves from provenance (high confidence) AND stdout/stdin is a TTY AND not `CI`/`ACCESSIBLE` weirdness, replace the "Run X to update" line with a `huh.NewConfirm` "New version %s available. Update now? [Y/n]" — on yes, `exec.Command("sh","-c",cmd)` with stdio wired through, on success print "Re-run `entire …`". Fall back to today's print-only notice when provenance is missing or we're non-interactive (don't auto-run a curl-pipe-bash we only guessed at).

Tradeoff: you're now running an installer mid-CLI-invocation, which can take 10-60s and, for `brew`/`scoop`, may prompt for passwords or touch shells the user didn't expect — codex gets away with it because the prompt is explicit and skippable. Safer variant: add `entire update` as a real subcommand that does the same exec, and have the notification say "press Y to run `entire update` now" so the heavy work is one layer removed and scriptable/testable on its own. Want me to sketch the `entire update` command + prompt wiring?

message.content: is there a way to have it like auto-update enable/disable and it checks from time to time (same as versionchecker) if there is a version and it just upgrades itself?

content.text:
Yes — add an `auto_update` setting (`off` | `prompt` | `auto`, default `prompt`) in global settings, read inside `CheckAndNotify` after the 24h cache gate. On `auto` + TTY + high-confidence provenance command: spawn the installer detached *after* the current command exits (register via `atexit`-style deferred goroutine or a `post-run` hook) so you never replace a binary mid-run, log outcome to `~/.config/entire/update.log`. Skip when `CI=1`, non-TTY, dev build, or command unresolved.

Tradeoff: `auto` trades consent for convenience — one bad release auto-lands on every machine overnight. Mitigate with a 24-48h "soak" delay (only auto-update versions ≥2 days old) and a `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` kill-switch. Want me to plan it?

content: Goal: add auto-update to the CLI like codex does, building on the in-progress install provenance work. Next: decide on an `auto_update` setting (off/prompt/auto, default prompt) with a soak delay and kill-switch, then plan the implementation. (disable recaps in /config)

# Plan: Auto-Update Mechanism for `entire` CLI

## Context

Today the CLI already detects outdated versions in `CheckAndNotify`
(`cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/versioncheck.go:23`) and prints a hint like
`brew upgrade entire`. An uncommitted change on this branch adds
`InstallProvenance` (`~/.config/entire/install.json`) so the hint maps to the
actual installer (install.sh / brew / scoop, stable | nightly).

Users want codex-style automation: the CLI should optionally run that installer
itself — either on confirmation (`prompt`) or silently (`auto`) — so a single
TTY keystroke is enough to stay current. Default must be **off** (opt-in) to
avoid surprise execution. Preference lives in a new global settings file at
`~/.config/entire/settings.json` so it is set once per machine, independent of
which repo you are standing in.

## Goal

1. New global settings file `~/.config/entire/settings.json` (loader + saver).
2. `auto_update` tri-state: `off` (default) | `prompt` | `auto`.
3. After the existing 24h version check fires and a newer version is detected,
   respect the mode and (on `auto`/`prompt`) run the installer command derived
   from `InstallProvenance`.
4. Subcommands: `entire auto-update {enable|disable|status|set <mode>}` and
   `entire update` (explicit one-shot, bypasses mode gate).
5. Guardrails: TTY required, not CI, provenance must resolve (no
   heuristic auto-run), release must be ≥24h old on `auto`, kill-switch env,
   retry throttle on failure.

## Design Overview

```
PersistentPostRun (root.go:44)
  └─ CheckAndNotify (versioncheck.go:23)
        └─ isOutdated == true
              └─ maybeAutoUpdate(ctx, w, current, latest, publishedAt)
                    ├─ loadGlobalSettings()          // ~/.config/entire/settings.json
                    ├─ gate: mode, TTY, CI, kill-switch, last-attempt, soak
                    ├─ resolve updateHint (provenance only for "auto")
                    ├─ mode=prompt → huh confirm (NewAccessibleForm)
                    └─ runInstaller(cmd) streaming stdout/stderr
```

Installer runs **synchronously inside `PersistentPostRun`** — the user's
command has already finished, so replacing the on-disk binary mid-run is safe
on Unix (open fd keeps old inode). Windows scoop handles locked binary via
pending-file-rename itself. No detach needed v1.

### Mode semantics

| Mode | Behavior when outdated |
|------|------------------------|
| `off` | Print current notification only (today's behavior). No prompt, no exec. |
| `prompt` | TTY + provenance OR fallback hint → `huh.Confirm` "Update now? [Y/n]". On yes, run installer. |
| `auto` | TTY + provenance resolved + release ≥24h old + no prior failure in last 24h → run installer silently (spinner + streamed output). |

### Global settings file

```json
{
  "auto_update": "off"
}
```

Minimal v1 schema; leave room for future global flags. Writes go through an
atomic temp-file + rename (mirror `saveCache` pattern at
`versioncheck.go:129-165`).

### Cache / throttle

Extend `VersionCache` (`versioncheck/types.go:6-8`) with
`LastUpdateAttemptTime time.Time` and `LastUpdateAttemptOk bool`. If the last
attempt failed within 24h, skip auto mode (prompt mode still runs — user
explicitly opted in each time).

### Kill switch

`ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` short-circuits `maybeAutoUpdate` before any work.
Documented in `--help` for `auto-update`.

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Global settings package

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/settings/global.go`

- `GlobalSettings` struct: `AutoUpdate string \`json:"auto_update,omitempty"\``
- Constants: `ModeOff = "off"`, `ModePrompt = "prompt"`, `ModeAuto = "auto"`.
- `LoadGlobal() (*GlobalSettings, error)` — reads `~/.config/entire/settings.json`; missing file returns defaults (`AutoUpdate: "off"`), not an error.
- `SaveGlobal(*GlobalSettings) error` — atomic temp-file + rename.
- `GlobalSettingsPath() (string, error)` — reuse `globalConfigDirPath` pattern from versioncheck (extract into a shared helper in settings package or new `cmd/entire/cli/paths/global.go`).

Kept separate from project `EntireSettings` — different lifecycle, different
location, avoids accidental merging.

### 2. Extend `VersionCache`

File: `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/types.go`

```go
type VersionCache struct {
    LastCheckTime          time.Time `json:"last_check_time"`
    LastUpdateAttemptTime  time.Time `json:"last_update_attempt_time,omitempty"`
    LastUpdateAttemptOk    bool      `json:"last_update_attempt_ok,omitempty"`
}
```

### 3. Add `PublishedAt` to GitHubRelease

File: `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/types.go` — add `PublishedAt time.Time \`json:"published_at"\``. Parse in `parseGitHubRelease`. Needed for soak delay.

### 4. New auto-update runner

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/autoupdate.go`

- `MaybeAutoUpdate(ctx, w, current, latest, publishedAt)` — the gate + runner.
- Uses `settings.LoadGlobal()`.
- TTY check via `term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdout.Fd()))`.
- CI check: `os.Getenv("CI") != ""`.
- Kill-switch: `os.Getenv("ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE") != ""`.
- Accessible prompt via `cli.NewAccessibleForm` → `huh.NewConfirm` (pattern at `cli/rewind.go:166`).
- `runInstaller(ctx, cmd string)` — `exec.CommandContext("sh","-c",cmd)` on unix, `cmd /C` on Windows; wire `Stdin/Stdout/Stderr` to the process streams. Return exit code. Record result in `VersionCache`.
- On `auto` mode, enforce `time.Since(publishedAt) >= 24*time.Hour`.
- For `auto`, require hint came from provenance (not path inference). Refactor `updateCommand()` to return `(hint string, fromProvenance bool)`.

### 5. Wire into `CheckAndNotify`

Edit `versioncheck.go:68-70`:

```go
if isOutdated(currentVersion, latestVersion) {
    printNotification(w, currentVersion, latestVersion)
    MaybeAutoUpdate(ctx, w, currentVersion, latestVersion, release.PublishedAt)
}
```

`CheckAndNotify` now needs the full `GitHubRelease`, not just the tag string.
Adjust `fetchLatestVersion`/`fetchLatestNightlyVersion` return types (they
currently return only a string — change to return `(*GitHubRelease, error)`
and keep the tag extraction in the caller).

### 6. `entire auto-update` subcommand

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/commands/auto_update.go`

```
entire auto-update status    # print current mode + config path + last attempt
entire auto-update enable    # set mode=prompt (sensible default opt-in)
entire auto-update disable   # set mode=off
entire auto-update set auto  # set mode=auto
```

Registered in `root.go:82-102`. Reads/writes via `settings.LoadGlobal` /
`SaveGlobal`. Use `NewSilentError` pattern (per CLAUDE.md error-handling
section) for friendly errors.

### 7. `entire update` subcommand

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/commands/update.go`

One-shot: force a check (ignoring 24h cache gate), resolve hint, run installer
with streamed output. Always runs regardless of `auto_update` mode. Flags:
`--check-only` (print hint, don't run), `--yes` (skip confirm).

### 8. Tests

Extend `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/versioncheck_test.go`:

- `TestMaybeAutoUpdate_ModeOff` — runs nothing even when outdated.
- `TestMaybeAutoUpdate_AutoRequiresProvenance` — heuristic fallback skipped on `auto`.
- `TestMaybeAutoUpdate_SoakDelay` — published <24h ago skipped on `auto`.
- `TestMaybeAutoUpdate_KillSwitch` — `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` short-circuits.
- `TestMaybeAutoUpdate_LastAttemptThrottle` — failed-within-24h skipped on `auto`.
- `TestMaybeAutoUpdate_PromptMode` — non-TTY path (confirm stub returns false → no exec).
- Override `runInstaller` via package-level `var runInstaller = realRunInstaller` to capture calls without spawning real processes (same pattern as `executablePath`).

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/settings/global_test.go` — round-trip for
`LoadGlobal`/`SaveGlobal` + default-on-missing.

New files for commands: `commands/auto_update_test.go`, `commands/update_test.go`.

## Guardrails

- `dev`/`""` version → skip (already in `CheckAndNotify`).
- Non-TTY stdin or stdout → skip auto-update (print hint only).
- `CI=1` → skip.
- `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` → skip.
- `auto` mode requires: provenance-resolved hint, published ≥24h, no failure in last 24h.
- Never call `os/exec` with `curl | bash` unless mode is `prompt` (explicit user consent) or provenance says `install.sh`.
- No `--amend`, no force-push, no destructive ops anywhere in the flow.

## Files Touched

New:
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/global.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/global_test.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/autoupdate.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/autoupdate_test.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/commands/auto_update.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/commands/auto_update_test.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/commands/update.go`
- `cmd/entire/cli/commands/update_test.go`
- `docs/architecture/auto-update.md` (brief user-facing doc; matches existing `install-provenance.md`)

Modified:
- `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/types.go` — extend `VersionCache`, add `PublishedAt`.
- `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/versioncheck.go` — refactor `updateCommand` return, fetchers return `*GitHubRelease`, wire `MaybeAutoUpdate`.
- `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/versioncheck_test.go` — update existing tests for new signatures.
- `cmd/entire/cli/root.go` — register `auto-update` + `update` subcommands.
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` — only if `GlobalSettingsPath` helper lives here.

## Verification

1. **Unit tests**: `mise run test` — must pass. Coverage for every guardrail listed.
2. **Integration**: `mise run test:integration` — no new integration tests required; existing root.go post-run behavior must still pass.
3. **Lint & fmt**: `mise run fmt && mise run lint` (required per CLAUDE.md before commit).
4. **Manual smoke (Unix, brew install)**:
   - `entire auto-update status` → "mode: off".
   - `entire auto-update enable` → "mode: prompt".
   - Set `~/.config/entire/version_check.json` LastCheckTime to >24h ago, stub `~/.config/entire/install.json` with `{"manager":"brew","channel":"stable","package":"entire"}`, run `entire version` against a mock GitHub releases URL via `ENTIRE_GITHUB_API_URL` (if unsupported, temp-patch in dev build) → should print notification and prompt.
   - Answer Y → `brew upgrade entire` runs, streams output.
   - `entire auto-update disable` → prompts stop.
   - `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 entire version` → no prompt even with mode=prompt.
5. **Manual `entire update`**: run with outdated version + provenance → installer fires. With `--check-only` → prints command, exits 0.
6. **CI skip**: `CI=1 entire version` → no prompt.
7. **Windows (if available)**: `entire auto-update enable`, trigger with scoop provenance → `cmd /C scoop update entire/cli` runs.

## Non-Goals (v1)

- Not implementing self-built binary download + atomic swap. We shell out to the native installer so brew/scoop/install.sh own the replacement.
- Not supporting `mise` auto-update (provenance today doesn't cover it; path heuristic exists but is fallback-only, so `auto` mode will skip. `mise` users keep the existing notification.)
- Not adding nightly `install.sh` support (scripts/install.sh is stable-only). Add when a nightly installer script ships.
- No background / daemon process — only runs during a foreground CLI invocation's `PersistentPostRun`.

# Plan: Auto-Update Mechanism for `entire` CLI

## Context

Today the CLI already detects outdated versions in `CheckAndNotify`
(`cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/versioncheck.go:23`) and prints a hint like
`brew upgrade entire`. An uncommitted change on this branch adds
`InstallProvenance` (`~/.config/entire/install.json`) so the hint maps to the
actual installer (install.sh / brew / scoop, stable | nightly).

Users want codex-style automation: the CLI should optionally run that installer
itself — either on confirmation (`prompt`) or silently (`auto`) — so a single
TTY keystroke is enough to stay current. Default must be **off** (opt-in) to
avoid surprise execution. Preference lives in a new global settings file at
`~/.config/entire/settings.json` so it is set once per machine, independent of
which repo you are standing in.

## Goal

1. New global settings file `~/.config/entire/settings.json` (loader + saver).
2. `auto_update` tri-state: `off` (default) | `prompt` | `auto`.
3. After the existing 24h version check fires and a newer version is detected,
   respect the mode and (on `auto`/`prompt`) run the installer command derived
   from `InstallProvenance`.
4. Subcommands: `entire auto-update {enable|disable|status|set <mode>}` and
   `entire update` (explicit one-shot, bypasses mode gate).
5. Guardrails: TTY required, not CI, provenance must resolve (no
   heuristic auto-run), release must be ≥24h old on `auto`, kill-switch env,
   retry throttle on failure.

## Design Overview

```
PersistentPostRun (root.go:44)
  └─ CheckAndNotify (versioncheck.go:23)
        └─ isOutdated == true
              └─ maybeAutoUpdate(ctx, w, current, latest, publishedAt)
                    ├─ loadGlobalSettings()          // ~/.config/entire/settings.json
                    ├─ gate: mode, TTY, CI, kill-switch, last-attempt, soak
                    ├─ resolve updateHint (provenance only for "auto")
                    ├─ mode=prompt → huh confirm (NewAccessibleForm)
                    └─ runInstaller(cmd) streaming stdout/stderr
```

Installer runs **synchronously inside `PersistentPostRun`** — the user's
command has already finished, so replacing the on-disk binary mid-run is safe
on Unix (open fd keeps old inode). Windows scoop handles locked binary via
pending-file-rename itself. No detach needed v1.

### Mode semantics

| Mode | Behavior when outdated |
|------|------------------------|
| `off` | Print current notification only (today's behavior). No prompt, no exec. |
| `prompt` | TTY + provenance OR fallback hint → `huh.Confirm` "Update now? [Y/n]". On yes, run installer. |
| `auto` | TTY + provenance resolved + release ≥24h old + no prior failure in last 24h → run installer silently (spinner + streamed output). |

### Global settings file

```json
{
  "auto_update": "off"
}
```

Minimal v1 schema; leave room for future global flags. Writes go through an
atomic temp-file + rename (mirror `saveCache` pattern at
`versioncheck.go:129-165`).

### Cache / throttle

Extend `VersionCache` (`versioncheck/types.go:6-8`) with
`LastUpdateAttemptTime time.Time` and `LastUpdateAttemptOk bool`. If the last
attempt failed within 24h, skip auto mode (prompt mode still runs — user
explicitly opted in each time).

### Kill switch

`ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` short-circuits `maybeAutoUpdate` before any work.
Documented in `--help` for `auto-update`.

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Global settings package

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/settings/global.go`

- `GlobalSettings` struct: `AutoUpdate string \`json:"auto_update,omitempty"\``
- Constants: `ModeOff = "off"`, `ModePrompt = "prompt"`, `ModeAuto = "auto"`.
- `LoadGlobal() (*GlobalSettings, error)` — reads `~/.config/entire/settings.json`; missing file returns defaults (`AutoUpdate: "off"`), not an error.
- `SaveGlobal(*GlobalSettings) error` — atomic temp-file + rename.
- `GlobalSettingsPath() (string, error)` — reuse `globalConfigDirPath` pattern from versioncheck (extract into a shared helper in settings package or new `cmd/entire/cli/paths/global.go`).

Kept separate from project `EntireSettings` — different lifecycle, different
location, avoids accidental merging.

### 2. Extend `VersionCache`

File: `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/types.go`

```go
type VersionCache struct {
    LastCheckTime          time.Time `json:"last_check_time"`
    LastUpdateAttemptTime  time.Time `json:"last_update_attempt_time,omitempty"`
    LastUpdateAttemptOk    bool      `json:"last_update_attempt_ok,omitempty"`
}
```

### 3. Add `PublishedAt` to GitHubRelease

File: `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/types.go` — add `PublishedAt time.Time \`json:"published_at"\``. Parse in `parseGitHubRelease`. Needed for soak delay.

### 4. New auto-update runner

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/autoupdate.go`

- `MaybeAutoUpdate(ctx, w, current, latest, publishedAt)` — the gate + runner.
- Uses `settings.LoadGlobal()`.
- TTY check via `term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdout.Fd()))`.
- CI check: `os.Getenv("CI") != ""`.
- Kill-switch: `os.Getenv("ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE") != ""`.
- Accessible prompt via `cli.NewAccessibleForm` → `huh.NewConfirm` (pattern at `cli/rewind.go:166`).
- `runInstaller(ctx, cmd string)` — `exec.CommandContext("sh","-c",cmd)` on unix, `cmd /C` on Windows; wire `Stdin/Stdout/Stderr` to the process streams. Return exit code. Record result in `VersionCache`.
- On `auto` mode, enforce `time.Since(publishedAt) >= 24*time.Hour`.
- For `auto`, require hint came from provenance (not path inference). Refactor `updateCommand()` to return `(hint string, fromProvenance bool)`.

### 5. Wire into `CheckAndNotify`

Edit `versioncheck.go:68-70`:

```go

    printNotification(w, currentVersion, latestVersion)
    MaybeAutoUpdate(ctx, w, currentVersion, latestVersion, release.PublishedAt)
}
```

`CheckAndNotify` now needs the full `GitHubRelease`, not just the tag string.

content: Auto mode lets Claude handle permission prompts automatically — Claude checks each tool call for risky actions and prompt injection before executing. Actions Claude identifies as safe are executed, while actions Claude identifies as risky are blocked and Claude may try a different approach. Ideal for long-running tasks. Sessions are slightly more expensive. Claude can make mistakes that allow harmful commands to run, it's recommended to only use in isolated environments. Shift+Tab to change mode.

input.content:
# Auto-Update

The Entire CLI can offer or install new releases automatically after its daily
version check. The feature is **off by default** and opt-in.

## Configuration

Settings live at `~/.config/entire/settings.json` (machine-wide, not
per-repository):

```json
{
  "auto_update": "prompt"
}
```

Values:

- `off` (default) — show the notification only; no prompt, no execution.
- `prompt` — after the notification, ask the user to confirm and run the installer on yes.
- `auto` — install silently when guardrails pass (see below).

### CLI subcommands

```
entire auto-update status              # print current mode + config path
entire auto-update enable              # set mode to "prompt"
entire auto-update disable             # set mode to "off"
entire auto-update set <off|prompt|auto>
```

### Manual update

```
entire update              # resolve installer, prompt Y/N, run it
entire update --yes        # skip confirmation
entire update --check-only # print the installer command without running it
```

## Guardrails

The auto-update path refuses to execute unless all of the following hold:

- `auto_update` is `prompt` or `auto`.
- stdout is a terminal.
- `CI` environment variable is empty.
- `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` environment variable is empty (kill switch).

Additionally, `auto` mode requires:

- An `InstallProvenance` file at `~/.config/entire/install.json` resolves to a
  known installer (brew / scoop / install.sh). The executable-path fallback is
  not trusted for silent installs.
- The release was published at least 24 hours ago (soak delay — cushion
  against a bad release).
- No failed attempt was recorded in the last 24 hours.

## Installer mapping

Derived from `InstallProvenance` (see `docs/architecture/install-provenance.md`):

- `install.sh` + `stable` → `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
- `brew` + `stable|nightly` → `brew upgrade <package>`
- `scoop` + `stable|nightly` → `scoop update <package>`

The installer is run via `sh -c` on Unix and `cmd /C` on Windows. stdin,
stdout, and stderr are wired to the user so passwords and progress output
flow through.

## Failure handling

Failed attempts are recorded in `~/.config/entire/version_check.json`.
In `auto` mode the CLI backs off for 24 hours after a failure; `prompt` mode
always re-prompts on the next run.

# Ship Changes

Commit current changes, push to remote, and update the PR.

## Step 1: Analyze changes

1. Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to understand what changed
2. Run `git status` to see untracked files
3. Run `git log --oneline -3` to match the repo's commit message style

## Step 2: Commit

1. Stage only the relevant changed/untracked files by name (never `git add -A` or `git add .`)
2. Write a concise commit message that focuses on the "why" not the "what"
   - If `draft` is provided, use it as the commit message
   - Otherwise, draft one from the diff
3. Commit. If hooks fail, diagnose and fix — do NOT use `--no-verify`

## Step 3: Push

1. Check if the branch tracks a remote: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`
2. If not tracking, push with `-u origin <branch>`
3. If tracking, just `git push`
4. If push is rejected (remote has new commits), pull with rebase first then push

## Step 4: Update PR

1. Find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr view --json number,body,title`
2. If no PR exists, skip this step and inform the user
3. Compare the current PR body against the new changes:
   - If the changes are within the existing PR scope, update the description to reflect the current state

5. When adding a comment, keep it concise — bullet points of what changed and why

Commit pushed. Draft PR body — preview before I open it:

**Title:** `Add auto-update feature behind opt-in global setting`

**Body:**
```markdown
## Summary
- New global settings file `~/.config/entire/settings.json` with `auto_update` tri-state: `off` (default), `prompt`, `auto`.
- After the existing daily version check flags an outdated release, the CLI prints the usual notification, then (mode-gated) prompts Y/N or installs silently.
- `entire auto-update {status|enable|disable|set <mode>}` manages the flag; `entire update [--yes] [--check-only]` runs the installer on demand.
- `install.sh` now writes install provenance to `~/.config/entire/install.json` so "auto" mode can trust the resolved installer command (brew / scoop / install.sh). Legacy executable-path heuristic remains as a fallback for notification-only.
- Guardrails: TTY + non-CI + kill-switch (`ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`) required. `auto` additionally requires provenance-resolved command, a 24h release soak, and 24h backoff after any failure.

## Test plan
- [x] `mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean
- [x] `mise run test:ci` green (unit + integration + canary)
- [x] Smoke: `entire auto-update status|enable|set auto|set bogus` (rejects invalid)
- [x] Smoke: `entire update --check-only` prints resolved command
- [x] Smoke: `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 entire update --yes` blocks
- [ ] Manual end-to-end on a real outdated brew install (reviewer)
- [ ] Windows scoop path verification (deferred)

## Non-goals (v1)
- No self-built binary download + atomic swap — we shell out to the native installer.
- No `mise` auto-update (path heuristic only; `auto` skips).
- No nightly `install.sh` channel (script is stable-only today).
- No background daemon — runs only during `PersistentPostRun` of a foreground invocation.

See `docs/architecture/auto-update.md` and `docs/architecture/install-provenance.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

1	# Entire - CLI
2	
3	This repo contains the CLI for Entire.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh
8	
9	## Key Directories
10	
11	### Commands (`cmd/`)
12	
13	- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point
14	- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers
15	- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
16	- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
17	- `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
18	- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (temporary and committed)
19	- `entire/cli/session`: session state management
20	- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
21	- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))
22	
23	## Tech Stack
24	
25	- Language: Go 1.26.x
26	- Build tool: mise, go modules
27	- Linting: golangci-lint
28	
29	## Development
30	
31	### Running Tests
32	
33	```bash
34	mise run test
35	```
36	
37	### Running Integration Tests
38	
39	```bash
40	mise run test:integration
41	```
42	
43	### Running All Tests (CI)
44	
45	```bash
46	mise run test:ci
47	```
48	
49	This runs unit tests, integration tests, and the E2E canary (Vogon agent) in sequence. Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
50	
51	### Running E2E Canary Tests (Vogon Agent)
52	
53	The Vogon agent is a deterministic fake agent that exercises the full E2E test suite without making any API calls. Named after the Vogons from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy — bureaucratic, procedural, and deterministic to a fault.
54	
55	```bash
56	mise run test:e2e:canary           # Run all E2E tests with the Vogon agent
57	mise run test:e2e:canary TestFoo   # Run a specific test
58	```
59	
60	- **Runs as part of `test:ci`** — canary failures block merges
61	- **No API calls, no cost** — safe to run freely, unlike real agent E2E tests
62	- **If a canary test fails, the bug is in the CLI or test infrastructure**, not in an agent
63	- Located in `e2e/vogon/` (binary) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/vogon/` (Agent interface)
64	- The binary parses prompts via regex, creates/modifies/deletes files, and fires lifecycle hooks
65	- **IMPORTANT: When changing E2E test prompt wording**, the Vogon binary (`e2e/vogon/main.go`) parses prompts with hardcoded regexes. New phrasing may not match existing patterns — always run `mise run test:e2e:canary` after changing prompt text and fix Vogon's parsing if tests fail.
66	
67	### Running E2E Tests (Only When Explicitly Requested)
68	
69	**IMPORTANT: Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** E2E tests make real API calls to agents, which consume tokens and cost money. Only run them when the user explicitly asks for E2E testing.
70	
71	```bash
72	mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # All agents, filtered
73	mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only
74	mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli [filter]        # Gemini CLI only
75	mise run test:e2e --agent opencode [filter]          # OpenCode only
76	mise run test:e2e --agent cursor [filter]            # Cursor only
77	mise run test:e2e --agent factoryai-droid [filter]   # Factory AI Droid only
78	mise run test:e2e --agent copilot-cli [filter]       # Copilot CLI only
79	```
80	
81	E2E tests:
82	
83	- Use the `//go:build e2e` build tag
84	- Located in `e2e/tests/`
85	- See [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) for full documentation (structure, debugging, adding agents)
86	- Test real agent interactions (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, or Vogon creating files, committing, etc.)
87	- Validate checkpoint scenarios documented in `docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md`
88	- Support multiple agents via `E2E_AGENT` env var (`claude-code`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `copilot-cli`, `vogon`)
89	
90	**Environment variables:**
91	
92	- `E2E_AGENT` - Agent to test with (default: `claude-code`)
93	- `E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` - Claude model to use (default: `haiku` for cost efficiency)
94	- `E2E_TIMEOUT` - Timeout per prompt (default: `2m`)
95	
96	### Test Parallelization
97	
98	**Always use `t.Parallel()` in tests.** Every top-level test function and subtest should call `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state (e.g., `os.Chdir()`).
99	
100	```go
101	func TestFeature_Foo(t *testing.T) {
102	    t.Parallel()
103	    // ...
104	}
105	
106	// Integration tests with TestEnv
107	func TestFeature_Bar(t *testing.T) {
108	    t.Parallel()
109	    env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
110	    // ...
111	}
112	```
113	
114	**Exception:** Tests that modify process-global state cannot be parallelized. This includes `os.Chdir()`/`t.Chdir()` and `os.Setenv()`/`t.Setenv()` — Go's test framework will panic if these are used after `t.Parallel()`.
115	
116	### Git in Tests
117	
118	**Tests that touch git state must use an isolated temp repo — never the real repo CWD.**
119	
120	Many handlers (lifecycle, strategy, hooks) resolve the git repo from CWD via `OpenRepository`, `GetGitCommonDir`, `DetectFileChanges`, etc. Without isolation, tests can create session state files, shadow branches, or other artifacts in the real `.git/` directory.
121	
122	Use the `testutil` helpers:
123	
124	```go
125	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
126	testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)                    // git init + user config + disable GPG
127	testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "f.txt", "init")  // create a file
128	testutil.GitAdd(t, tmpDir, "f.txt")             // stage it
129	testutil.GitCommit(t, tmpDir, "init")           // commit (needs at least one commit for HEAD)
130	t.Chdir(tmpDir)                                 // redirect CWD-based git resolution
131	```
132	
133	`testutil.InitRepo` configures `user.name`, `user.email`, and disables GPG signing — safe for CI environments without global git config.
134	
135	**Prefer `testutil.InitRepo()` over direct `git.PlainInit()` in tests.** When a test in this repo needs an initialized repository, use `testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)` unless the test specifically needs lower-level initialization behavior that the helper cannot provide. Do not call `git.PlainInit()` directly and then create commits or run CLI git operations without also reproducing the helper's repo-local config.
136	
137	**Do NOT** shell out to `git init`/`git commit` directly without setting user config and `--no-gpg-sign`, and **do NOT** run lifecycle/strategy handlers from the real repo CWD in tests.
138	
139	### Linting and Formatting
140	
141	```bash
142	mise run fmt && mise run lint
143	```
144	
145	`mise run fmt` can rewrite files. Treat `mise run fmt && mise run lint` as a single verification sequence: if formatting changes anything, run lint again on the formatted tree rather than assuming a previous lint result still applies.
146	
147	### Before Every Commit (REQUIRED)

153	```

165	Safety note: do not treat a clean `mise run lint` result as final unless it was run after the most recent `mise run fmt` pass.

set -euo pipefail

GITHUB_REPO="entireio/cli"

DEFAULT_CHANNEL="stable"

# Colors (disabled in non-interactive mode)
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    RED='\033[0;31m'
    GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
    BLUE='\033[0;34m'
    BOLD='\033[1m'
    NC='\033[0m' # No Color
else
    RED=''
    GREEN=''
    YELLOW=''
    BLUE=''
    BOLD=''
    NC=''
fi

info() {
    printf '%b%s%b\n' "${BLUE}==>${NC} ${BOLD}" "$1" "${NC}"
}

success() {
    printf '%b%s%b\n' "${GREEN}==>${NC} ${BOLD}" "$1" "${NC}"
}

warn() {
    printf '%b %s\n' "${YELLOW}Warning:${NC}" "$1"
}

error() {
    printf '%b %s\n' "${RED}Error:${NC}" "$1" >&2
    exit 1
}

usage() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: install.sh [--channel stable|nightly]

Options:
  --channel   Release channel to install (default: stable)
  -h, --help  Show this help message
EOF
}

detect_os() {
    local os
    os="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    case "$os" in
        darwin)
            echo "darwin"
            ;;
        linux)
            echo "linux"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported operating system: $os"
            ;;
    esac
}

detect_arch() {
    local arch
    arch="$(uname -m)"
    case "$arch" in
        x86_64|amd64)
            echo "amd64"
            ;;
        arm64|aarch64)
            echo "arm64"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported architecture: $arch"

# Auto-Update

The Entire CLI can offer or install new releases automatically after its daily
version check. The feature is **off by default** and opt-in.

## Configuration

Settings live at `~/.config/entire/settings.json` (machine-wide, not
per-repository):

```json
{
  "auto_update": "prompt"
}
```

Values:

- `off` (default) — show the notification only; no prompt, no execution.
- `prompt` — after the notification, ask the user to confirm and run the installer on yes.
- `auto` — install silently when guardrails pass (see below).

### CLI subcommands

```
entire auto-update status              # print current mode + config path
entire auto-update enable              # set mode to "prompt"
entire auto-update disable             # set mode to "off"
entire auto-update set <off|prompt|auto>
```

### Manual update

```
entire update              # resolve installer, prompt Y/N, run it
entire update --yes        # skip confirmation
entire update --check-only # print the installer command without running it
```

## Guardrails

The auto-update path refuses to execute unless all of the following hold:

- `auto_update` is `prompt` or `auto`.
- stdout is a terminal.
- `CI` environment variable is empty.
- `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` environment variable is empty (kill switch).

Additionally, `auto` mode requires:

- `installManagerForCurrentBinary()` resolves to a known manager (brew, mise,
  scoop). The curl fallback is not trusted for silent installs.
- The release was published at least 24 hours ago (soak delay — cushion
  against a bad release).
- No failed attempt was recorded in the last 24 hours.

## Installer mapping

Derived from the running binary's path plus the release channel
(stable / nightly). See `versioncheck.updateCommand` for the authoritative
table.

- Homebrew / Homebrew cask → `brew upgrade --cask entire[@nightly]`
- mise → `mise upgrade entire`
- scoop → `scoop update entire/cli`
- unknown → `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash [-s -- --channel nightly]`

The installer is run via `sh -c` on Unix and `cmd /C` on Windows. stdin,
stdout, and stderr are wired to the user so passwords and progress output
flow through.

## Failure handling

Failed attempts are recorded in `~/.config/entire/version_check.json`.
In `auto` mode the CLI backs off for 24 hours after a failure; `prompt` mode
always re-prompts on the next run.

content.text:
Local test recipe. Assumes TTY shell (not inside this harness).

**1. Build fake-old binary (bypass version skip):**
```
go build -ldflags="-X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version=v0.1.0" -o /tmp/entire ./cmd/entire
```

**2. Clean HOME so you don't clobber real cache:**
```
export H=$(mktemp -d)
```

**3. Subcommand smoke (works without network):**
```
HOME=$H /tmp/entire auto-update status            # -> off
HOME=$H /tmp/entire auto-update enable            # -> prompt
HOME=$H /tmp/entire auto-update set auto          # -> auto
HOME=$H /tmp/entire auto-update set bogus         # rejects
HOME=$H /tmp/entire update --check-only           # prints resolved command
HOME=$H ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 /tmp/entire update --yes   # kill-switch blocks
```

**4. Trigger the post-command auto-update flow (needs real TTY + network):**
```
HOME=$H /tmp/entire auto-update enable             # mode=prompt
rm -f $H/.config/entire/version_check.json         # force fetch next run
HOME=$H /tmp/entire version                        # hits GitHub API, sees v0.1.0 < latest, prompts Y/N
```

Answer N and rerun to iterate. Delete the cache file each time — `CheckAndNotify` writes it every invocation to gate the 24h check.

**5. Auto mode (silent install).** Only fires when `installManagerForCurrentBinary()` returns known (brew/mise/scoop). A bare `/tmp/entire` binary won't match — it resolves `unknown` and auto mode skips. Two ways to exercise it:
- Copy the binary into a path that matches, e.g. `mkdir -p /tmp/fake/Cellar/entire/0/bin && cp /tmp/entire /tmp/fake/Cellar/entire/0/bin/entire && /tmp/fake/Cellar/entire/0/bin/entire auto-update set auto`. Then repeat step 4 with that path.
- Or just run the unit tests: `go test -run Auto ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/ -v`.

**6. Soak-delay + retry-cooldown.** The release must be ≥24h old (real GitHub releases satisfy this). Retry cooldown is tested via `TestMaybeAutoUpdate_AutoRetryCooldown` — hard to simulate manually without poking `version_check.json`.

**Gotchas:**
- `PersistentPostRun` runs for *any* entire subcommand; avoid running `/tmp/entire` inside a non-TTY pipe when iterating.
- `CI=1` in your env short-circuits. Check with `echo $CI`.
- Dev builds (`version=="dev"`) skip — that's why step 1 uses `-ldflags` to set a real-looking version.

content.text:
Fair challenge. Current shape: 2 subcommands + global settings file + tri-state + soak/retry bookkeeping. Most of it is defensive against silent auto install. If we drop silent, 90% of the code disappears.

**Simplest viable (codex-shape):**
- No subcommands. No settings file. No tri-state.
- When `CheckAndNotify` detects outdated + TTY + no `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` → inline `huh.Confirm` "Update now? Y/n".
- On yes: `sh -c updateCommand(currentVersion)`.
- On no: do nothing, 24h cache already suppresses re-prompt.
- Kill switch env stops it entirely for users who never want the prompt.

Delete:
- `cmd/entire/cli/auto_update.go` + test
- `cmd/entire/cli/update.go` + test
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/global.go` + test
- `VersionCache.LastUpdateAttempt*` fields + `recordUpdateAttempt`
- `autoUpdateSoakDuration` + `autoUpdateRetryCooldown`
- `MaybeAutoUpdate` mode branching
- Docs section about modes + subcommands

Keep:
- `MaybeAutoUpdate` (thin: TTY + env gates + confirm + exec)
- `runInstaller` + test seam
- `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` kill switch
- `GitHubRelease.PublishedAt` — actually drop, not needed without soak

**Mental diff:** autoupdate.go shrinks ~80→~30 lines. types.go unchanged vs main. No new files. PR goes from ~15 files to ~2 modified.

**Tradeoff give-up:**
- No silent auto install. Power user who wants zero-friction can still alias `yes | entire` or write their own cron.
- No "don't ask again" persistence (beyond kill switch). 24h cache means at most one prompt/day, so low noise.
- No `entire update` one-shot — but notification + prompt covers it.

**Even-thinner variant:** skip `huh.Confirm` entirely. Just add to the notification: "Press Enter to update or Ctrl-C to skip" — read one byte from stdin. Cuts `huh` dep. Worse UX for N though (hitting Enter = yes is surprising). Not recommended.

# Auto-Update

After the Entire CLI's daily version check detects a newer release, the
standard notification is followed by an interactive Y/N prompt to run the
installer.

## UX

```
A newer version of Entire CLI is available: v1.2.3 (current: v1.0.0)
Run 'brew upgrade --cask entire' to update.

? Install the new version now?  (Y/n)
```

- Declining simply skips the upgrade. The 24-hour version-check cache means
  the prompt will not reappear until the next day.
- The installer command is whatever `versioncheck.updateCommand(current)`
  returns — `brew upgrade --cask ...`, `mise upgrade entire`,
  `scoop update entire/cli`, or the curl-pipe-bash fallback — including the
  `--channel nightly` variant for nightly builds.
- stdin, stdout and stderr are wired through so the user sees installer
  output and can answer any password prompt.

## Guardrails

The prompt is skipped silently when any of the following holds:

- stdout is not a terminal.
- `CI` environment variable is set.
- `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` environment variable is set (kill switch).

In those cases the user still sees the existing notification line pointing
to the installer command.

## Not in scope

- No "silent auto-install" mode — the prompt is always interactive.
- No persisted preference — the kill-switch env is the escape hatch.
- No dedicated `entire auto-update` / `entire update` subcommands; the
  notification + prompt replaces them.

# Auto-Update

The Entire CLI can offer or install new releases automatically after its daily
version check. The feature is **off by default** and opt-in.

## Configuration

Settings live at `~/.config/entire/settings.json` (machine-wide, not
per-repository):

```json
{
  "auto_update": "prompt"
}
```

Values:

- `off` (default) — show the notification only; no prompt, no execution.
- `prompt` — after the notification, ask the user to confirm and run the installer on yes.
- `auto` — install silently when guardrails pass (see below).

### CLI subcommands

```
entire auto-update status              # print current mode + config path
entire auto-update enable              # set mode to "prompt"
entire auto-update disable             # set mode to "off"
entire auto-update set <off|prompt|auto>
```

### Manual update

```
entire update              # resolve installer, prompt Y/N, run it
entire update --yes        # skip confirmation
entire update --check-only # print the installer command without running it
```

## Guardrails

The auto-update path refuses to execute unless all of the following hold:

- `auto_update` is `prompt` or `auto`.
- stdout is a terminal.
- `CI` environment variable is empty.
- `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` environment variable is empty (kill switch).

Additionally, `auto` mode requires:

- `installManagerForCurrentBinary()` resolves to a known manager (brew, mise,
  scoop). The curl fallback is not trusted for silent installs.
- The release was published at least 24 hours ago (soak delay — cushion
  against a bad release).
- No failed attempt was recorded in the last 24 hours.

## Installer mapping

Derived from the running binary's path plus the release channel
(stable / nightly). See `versioncheck.updateCommand` for the authoritative
table.

- Homebrew / Homebrew cask → `brew upgrade --cask entire[@nightly]`
- mise → `mise upgrade entire`
- scoop → `scoop update entire/cli`
- unknown → `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash [-s -- --channel nightly]`

The installer is run via `sh -c` on Unix and `cmd /C` on Windows. stdin,
stdout, and stderr are wired to the user so passwords and progress output
flow through.

## Failure handling

Failed attempts are recorded in `~/.config/entire/version_check.json`.
In `auto` mode the CLI backs off for 24 hours after a failure; `prompt` mode
always re-prompts on the next run.

content.content:
## Summary
- New global settings file `~/.config/entire/settings.json` with `auto_update` tri-state: `off` (default), `prompt`, `auto`.
- After the existing daily version check flags an outdated release, the CLI prints the usual notification, then (mode-gated) prompts Y/N or installs silently.
- `entire auto-update {status|enable|disable|set <mode>}` manages the flag; `entire update [--yes] [--check-only]` runs the installer on demand.
- `install.sh` now writes install provenance to `~/.config/entire/install.json` so "auto" mode can trust the resolved installer command (brew / scoop / install.sh). Legacy executable-path heuristic remains as a fallback for notification-only.

content.text:
**1. Build fake-old binary:**
```
go build -ldflags="-X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version=v0.1.0" -o /tmp/entire ./cmd/entire
```

**2. Clean HOME:**
```
export H=$(mktemp -d)
```

**3. Trigger prompt (real TTY + network):**
```
HOME=$H /tmp/entire version
```
Output:
```
A newer version of Entire CLI is available: vX.Y.Z (current: v0.1.0)
Run 'curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash' to update.

? Install the new version now?  (Y/n)
```
- Answer **N** → nothing runs, exits 0.
- Answer **Y** → installer fires. On a plain binary it'll curl-pipe-bash; skip unless you want the real install. For brew/scoop shape, see step 5.

**4. Re-trigger (cache gates to once/day):**
```
rm -f $H/.config/entire/version_check.json
HOME=$H /tmp/entire version
```

**5. Force a specific installer path without installing via brew:**
```
mkdir -p /tmp/fake/Cellar/entire/0/bin
cp /tmp/entire /tmp/fake/Cellar/entire/0/bin/entire
rm -f $H/.config/entire/version_check.json
HOME=$H /tmp/fake/Cellar/entire/0/bin/entire version
```
Notification + prompt now resolves to `brew upgrade --cask entire`. Say N unless you have brew + the cask installed.

**6. Kill switch:**
```
rm -f $H/.config/entire/version_check.json
HOME=$H ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 /tmp/entire version
```
Notification prints, **no prompt**.

**7. CI gate:**
```
rm -f $H/.config/entire/version_check.json
HOME=$H CI=1 /tmp/entire version
```
Same — notification only.

**8. Non-TTY gate (pipe):**
```
rm -f $H/.config/entire/version_check.json
HOME=$H /tmp/entire version | cat
```
Notification only; prompt skipped.

**9. Unit tests (no network, no build):**
```
go test -run MaybeAutoUpdate -v ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/
```
Covers TTY, CI, kill-switch, user-declines, happy path, installer failure.

**Gotchas:**
- Dev builds (`version=="dev"`) skip everything — `-ldflags` set in step 1 avoids this.
- `echo $CI` in your shell — unset it if set globally.
- `ACCESSIBLE=1` switches to a plain text prompt (works with screen readers).

**A. Version actually set?**

**B. Env set somewhere in your shell?**
```

```
Any match kills the prompt.

**C. The 2s GitHub timeout firing silently.** `CheckAndNotify` swallows every error. Test by pre-seeding a known-outdated latest via cache-bypass: easiest is to run twice — first run populates cache; on first run the prompt should appear. If network/API is slow or blocked, it won't. Check:
```

```
Must return JSON within 2s. If not, that's your blocker.

**D. Cache already present.** `mktemp -d` should be empty, but just verify:
```
ls -la $H/.config/entire/ 2>/dev/null
rm -rf $H/.config/entire
```

**E. See the silent debug log.** `CheckAndNotify` logs skips with `logging.Debug`, but only to `.entire/logs/entire.log` which needs a project repo. Easier: add one print to confirm flow — patch `versioncheck.go:68` temporarily:

}

Most likely: **A**. The Version path I gave might be wrong — confirm with `go tool nm /tmp/entire | grep versioninfo.Version` and paste the result.

content.text:
Confirmed end-to-end. Notification reaches the user; prompt itself skipped here because **my shell has no TTY**, but the code path to it is clean.

**Your blocker:** `api.github.com` returns `HTTP 403 rate limit exceeded` for your IP. `CheckAndNotify` silently treats any fetch error as "nothing to do", so no notification, no prompt. Confirmed with `curl -m 15 https://api.github.com/repos/entireio/cli/releases/latest` → `{"message":"API rate limit exceeded..."}`.

**Two fixes:**

**(a) Wait it out** — unauthenticated limit resets hourly. Try again in ~60 min.

**(b) Stub locally** (what I just did, works now):
```
mkdir -p /tmp/fakegh
printf '{"tag_name":"v99.0.0","prerelease":false}' > /tmp/fakegh/latest.json
(cd /tmp/fakegh && python3 -m http.server 9901 --bind 127.0.0.1 &)

go build \
  -ldflags="-X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version=v0.1.0 \
            -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck.githubAPIURL=http://127.0.0.1:9901/latest.json" \
  -o /tmp/entire ./cmd/entire

H=$(mktemp -d) HOME=$H /tmp/entire version
```

In your TTY shell you'll see the notification **and** the Y/N prompt. Kill the stub with `pkill -f "http.server 9901"` when done.

Product thought: we might want to surface fetch failures at least once so a user who never gets a prompt knows why. Either a minimal `"(version check unavailable)"` line, or flipping the `logging.Debug` to `logging.Warn`. Want me to add that?

content.text:
Hook blocked the force-push. Removing those commits from the remote branch requires rewriting remote history — no way around it with git.

**What I did locally:**
- Built a single clean commit on top of latest `origin/main` containing only the 5 auto-update files (`versioncheck/autoupdate.go`, `_test.go`, `versioncheck.go` wiring, `versioncheck_test.go`, `docs/architecture/auto-update.md`).
- Pointed `add-auto-aupdate` at it. Old history is still reachable via reflog.
- Verified build + test + lint green.

**What I need to do:**
- `git push --force-with-lease origin add-auto-aupdate` — replaces the remote branch contents and trims PR #981 down to just that one commit.

**Why `--force-with-lease` is safe here:**
- The PR is only yours; no other collaborators pushing to it.
- `--force-with-lease` aborts if remote moved (vs plain `--force`).
- Old commits remain in reflog locally for 30-90 days if we need to recover them.

**Alternative non-force path:** revert each unwanted commit with a new commit on top. Keeps history intact but PR grows to 5 commits (3 original + 2 reverts) and reviewers still see the noise in "Files changed". Worse UX.

## Summary
- When the existing daily version check flags an outdated release, the CLI prints the usual notification and then asks "Install the new version now? [Y/n]".
- Accepting runs whatever command `versioncheck.updateCommand(current)` resolves to (`brew upgrade --cask entire[@nightly]`, `mise upgrade entire`, `scoop update entire/cli`, or the curl-pipe-bash fallback). stdin/stdout/stderr stream through so installer prompts and progress reach the user.
- Declining skips the upgrade; the 24h version-check cache keeps the prompt from repeating more than once per day.
- Guardrails: stdout must be a TTY, `CI` must be empty, `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` is a kill switch.

## Test plan
- [x] `mise run check` green locally (unit + integration + canary)
- [x] Unit: TTY gate, CI gate, kill-switch, user-declines, happy path, installer failure
- [ ] Manual end-to-end on a real outdated brew install (reviewer)
- [ ] Windows scoop path verification (deferred)

## Non-goals
- No silent auto-install mode — prompt is always interactive.
- No persisted preference / subcommands — kill-switch env is the escape hatch.
- No self-built binary download; shells out to the native installer.

See `docs/architecture/auto-update.md`.

Replaces #981 (clean history — single commit on top of `main` with only the auto-update files).
